Jan. 11, 1907: William T. Wilson and Eliza W. Wilson sell James Keelty the southernmost part of the Wilson lots on the York Road, the ground Keelty leased out in 1907 as 2958's $65-rent lot (R.O. 2302/43)
Aug. 24, 1907: James Keelty leases James F. and Mary E. Bowersox the 14-foot lot at 2958 Greenmount for 99 years renewable forever at $65 a year, for $1,850 (S.C.L. 2363/423)

Aug. 24, 1907: James F. and Mary E. Bowersox mortgage the 14-foot lot at 2958 Greenmount to the Madison Square Permanent Building Association for $1,300, the balance of the purchase money (S.C.L. 2363/425; the end is not pulled)
Oct. 3, 1917: James Keelty and Nora L. Keelty convey the lot next north of 2958's leasehold, down to Thirtieth Street, to Alice E. Brandt in trust for the Bowersox family (S.C.L. 3159/384)

July 15, 1961: the Gerwig heirs sell Jerome and Lillian Silbiger 2958 Greenmount's fee and its $65 ground rent 'to the end and intent that the reversionary and leasehold estates be forever merged and the annual ground rent henceforth extinguished' (J.F.C. 1134/578)

Oct. 31, 1931: William H. Wolfe and Charles T. Leight convey the $180-rent leasehold they bought from Lula B. Dietrich in 1927 to Lula Smith, spinster, the first of two same-day steps that turn their tenancy in common into two tenancies by the entireties (S.C.L. 5263/428)

Oct. 31, 1931: Lula Smith conveys the $180-rent leasehold back in two halves, to William H. and Carrie Wolfe and to Charles T. and Ella B. Leight, each couple as tenants by the entireties (S.C.L. 5263/428 to 429)

Oct. 5, 1932: Charles T. Leight and Ella B. Leight deed William H. Flayhart Jr. and Catherine B. Flayhart the corner lot at 3020 Greenmount, the first of a same-day pair that puts it straight back in the Leights' names (S.C.L. 5328/110)
June 21, 1948: William H. and Carrie Wolfe assign Charles T. and Ella B. Leight their undivided half of the 3010 leasehold, $180 a year, for $5 (M.L.P. 7491/449)

Oct. 24, 1950: William H. and Carrie Wolfe sell Charles T. Leight, widower, the reversion and the $180 ground rent of 3010 Greenmount for $3,000 plus accrued rent, so that the lease merges into the fee (M.L.P. 8259/53)

Apr. 11, 1822: John McFadon conveys the Ensor's Inspection ground 'at or near the gate' to John W. Stump and Philip G. Biays in trust for Sarah Biays for life, then for her four daughters, for $7,700 (W.G. 165/492)

Aug. 2, 1954: Henry John Weber, Adam H. Weber and Raymond H. Plack and their wives lease Elizabeth McC. West the 3011 Greenmount lot, 99 years at $66 a year, and deed the reversion and the rent (M.L.P. 9546/140 to 142; only the last page is pulled)
Aug. 2, 1954: Elizabeth McC. West assigns Max Silen the 3011 Greenmount leasehold, 99 years renewable forever at $66 a year, for $5 (M.L.P. 9546/143)
Aug. 2, 1954: the Belair Road Building and Loan Association releases the Webers' and Placks' June 19, 1954 mortgage on 3011 Greenmount the day the lot is leased and sold (M.L.P. 9546/146)
Aug. 25, 1954: John E. Minor assigns Max Silen the 3013 Greenmount leasehold, 99 years renewable forever at one cent a year, for $5 (M.L.P. 9566/459)

Aug. 24, 1954: Charles F. and Alice F. Obrecht deed Samuel G. Silen the reversion and one-cent ground rent of 3013 Greenmount for $5, the day before Minor assigns the leasehold to Max Silen (M.L.P. 9566/461)
